svg.title: Python: start a local HTTP server.
svg.desc: Requires Bash and Python 3; missing tools refer to Package Management. An indented Bash example creates a new web-demo directory, writes index.html containing Hello, and starts Python's HTTP server bound to loopback port 8000. An existing directory prevents changes and startup. HOME, conditional execution and line continuation are decoded. Private files and links must stay out; local users can connect. This is for learning, not production hosting.
svg.text: PYTHON: START A LOCAL HTTP SERVER.
Serves web-demo files locally; / returns index.html containing Hello.
Requires Bash and python3. Missing? See Package Management / 01–02.
NEW directory only. Never serve your whole home, private files or links to them.
$HOME = your home. && starts the server only if writing the page succeeds.
\ continues the line. Ctrl-C stops this foreground server.
Existing directory? mkdir fails: nothing is changed or started.
127.0.0.1 binds to loopback: only this computer can connect.
Local users can connect. For learning, not public or production hosting.
